Bosom
booz'um
n. (the breast; the place of intimacy and safekeeping; rendering Hebrew cheq, Greek kolpos)
From the Saxon bosm. Hebrew cheq is the fold of the garment at the breast, where a shepherd carried a lamb and a man carried what was precious — so the word means the place of nearest keeping before it means a part of the body.

Biblical Definition

Bosom denotes the place of closest intimacy and safest keeping, and Scripture puts three of its greatest statements there. Of the Trinity: “No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him” (John 1:18) — the eternal nearness of the Son to the Father is the reason he can make the Father known, and revelation therefore rests on relation. Of God's care for the weakest of his flock: “He shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom” (Isaiah 40:11), where the strong arm that gathers and the bosom that carries belong to the same God who in the preceding verses measures the waters in the hollow of his hand. Of the state of the righteous dead before the resurrection: the beggar “died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom” (Luke 16:22), a phrase for blessed rest in the company of the father of the faithful. Proverbs uses the word for the folly of harboured sin: “Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burned?” (Proverbs 6:27) — what is carried closest will do the most damage.

Webster 1828 Definition

The fold at the breast — the place of intimacy and safekeeping. The Son is in the bosom of the Father; the Shepherd carries lambs in his; and Lazarus was carried into Abraham's.

expand to see more

BOSOM, n. s as z. [Sax. bosm.] The breast of a human being, and the parts adjacent.

2. The folds or covering of clothes about the breast; a place of safekeeping.

3. Embrace; inclosure; compass; as, in the bosom of the church.

4. Intimacy; nearest affection; as, a bosom friend.

5. In Scripture, the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, John 1; carried into Abraham's bosom, Luke 16.

Key Scripture

John 1:18 — "No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him."

Isaiah 40:11 — "He shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom, and shall gently lead those that are with young."

Luke 16:22 — "And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;"

Proverbs 6:27 — "Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burned?"

Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The word has faded from ordinary speech, and with it the picture of a shepherd carrying a lamb inside the fold of his robe.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The loss is imaginative. A modern reader hears bosom as archaic or awkward, and Isaiah 40:11 flattens into a general reassurance. The picture is specific: a shepherd's outer garment was gathered by a belt so that the fold across the chest formed a pouch, and a newborn or injured lamb travelled there, against the man's ribs, unable to walk and not required to. Isaiah places this immediately after the verses on God's incomparable greatness, and the juxtaposition is the point.

The principle to recover is what John 1:18 grounds. The Son who declares the Father is the Son who has eternally been in his bosom, so Christian revelation is not information relayed by a messenger but disclosure by one who has always been at the Father's side. That is why he can say he that hath seen me hath seen the Father. And Proverbs 6:27 supplies the sober counterweight, that the bosom is also where a man hides what will ruin him: sin cherished close is not contained by being hidden, and the clothes burn.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew cheq is the bosom or the fold of a garment, the place of carrying; chob is likewise the breast. Greek kolpos is the bosom, the fold of a robe, and by extension a bay or gulf.

expand to see more

Hebrew cheq (H2436) — bosom, the fold of the garment; where a shepherd carried a lamb.

Hebrew chob (H2243) — the bosom; used in Job of what is hidden in the breast.

Greek kolpos (G2859) — bosom, lap, the fold of a garment; also a bay of the sea.

Greek monogenes (G3439) — only begotten; the Son who is in the bosom of the Father.

Greek exegeomai (G1834) — to lead out, to declare fully; he hath declared him, John 1:18.

Usage

"Of the Son's eternal nearness as the ground of revelation: which is in the bosom of the Father (John 1:18)."

"Of the Shepherd's care for the weakest: he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom (Isaiah 40:11)."

"Of the blessed dead: was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom (Luke 16:22)."
